title: Google Review NFC Cards for Pickup Counters
summary: Pickup counter is a different beast from full-service checkout. The customer comes in expecting a fast handoff — restaurant takeout, BOPIS (Buy Online Pick-up In Store), curbside grocery, mobile-order coffee, prescription pickup. The window between bag-handoff and customer-walking-out is roughly 8–15 seconds, and the moment of peak satisfaction is the second the customer confirms the order is right. This page covers pickup-counter NFC review cards (counter card + bag-tag insert + curbside drive-up card) integrated with Toast / Olo / DoorDash / Uber Eats / Square Online / Shopify / Target / Walmart BOPIS workflows — operated within FTC 16 CFR Part 465 + Google Business Profile policy.
heroPoints: The peak conversion moment at pickup is order-confirmation handoff — the 3–5 seconds when customer verifies bag contents and turns to leave.
Bag-tag inserts attached to handle / stapled to receipt convert better than passive counter cards because pickup customers move fast and don't browse counter signage.
Curbside drive-up requires a different placement — runner-handed card or bag-clip, not a counter card, because customer never enters the building.

Pharmacy prescription pickup — CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid drive-thru + counter.
Apparel + footwear BOPIS — Nordstrom, Macy's, DSW, Foot Locker pickup zones.

brief.label: Pickup-counter placement geometry
items: Bag-handle hangtag — primary placement; tag tied or stapled to take-out bag handle / clipped to BOPIS bag.
Receipt-attachment card — small card stapled to receipt placed inside bag.
Order-shelf-front placement — counter card facing customer-side of pickup shelf (not staff-side).
Pickup-runner hand-off card — runner physically hands card with bag for curbside / drive-thru.
Drive-thru window card — curbside-vehicle handoff, runner places card on top of bag.
Curbside-bag-clip — small NFC clip attached to curbside-delivery bag handle.
BOPIS locker placement — sticker on locker door or insert in pickup envelope.
Avoid: counter-front passive placement (pickup customers don't browse), kitchen-side (staff-only zone).

brief.label: Runner / pickup-staff soft-skill prompt framework
items: Earn-the-right via fast accurate handoff — order completeness check before any prompt.
Time at peak: 3–5 second window after order verified + bag handed.
Bag-tag does the work: customer discovers card after leaving, removing in-counter awkwardness.
Verbal optional: 'Bag's all yours — there's a quick review tap on the bag if you have a sec' (low-pressure).
Curbside runner: hand bag through window + brief verbal at handoff; one-shot only.
Respect time pressure: pickup customers are time-pressed; never extend interaction.
Drive-thru: never ask at window; rely on bag-tag discovery in car / at home.
Track per-runner card-handoff completion rate for BOPIS shift staffing analytics.

brief.label: Bag-tag + card design principles
items: Restaurant takeout — durable PVC + grease-resistant + brand colours; tied to bag handle.
BOPIS retail — paper or PVC card stapled to receipt + tucked in bag.
Curbside grocery — laminated card or NFC clip resistant to refrigerated / cold-chain bag exposure.
Pharmacy pickup — generic copy (no prescription / medical context references) — HIPAA-aware.
Coffee mobile-order — small bag-clip variant; mobile-order pickup zone counter sign.
Furniture / bulky pickup — receipt-insert card; bag-tag impractical for boxed goods.
Hangtag string + reinforced punch hole for bag-handle attachment durability.
QR fallback printed alongside NFC for older demographics / non-NFC populations.
Removable adhesive variant — for stick-on bag-tag without damaging premium-bag finish.

brief.label: Multi-location chain + franchise operations
items: Per-store GBP audit + per-store review-link capture for pickup-counter URL.
Per-store card encoding routes reviews to correct location.
Per-shift / per-runner UTM (optional) — tracks BOPIS-runner contribution.
Brand-standard book + central marketing portal locked for franchise compliance.
Reorder cycle synced to brand-refresh + bag-supplier reorder cycle.
High-volume pickup chains: 15–30 % per-year replacement reserve (bag-tags lost / damaged).
Annual compliance audit: FTC + state-specific advertising rules + (HIPAA for pharmacy pickup).
Cross-buyer reference notes — restaurant, BOPIS retail, grocery, pharmacy and curbside programmes — best-practice sharing across pickup-counter cohorts.

brief.label: FTC + Google + HIPAA compliance framework
items: FTC 16 CFR Part 465 (effective Oct 21, 2024) — fake-review prohibition + Endorsement Guides.
Card copy: 'Thanks for picking up with us — tap if you have a moment to share' — never 'Leave 5 stars'.
Google Business Profile policy — no review-gating, no incentivisation.
Restaurant: cannot tie review request to free-side / discount-on-next-order programmes.
Curbside: runner verbal prompt offered to ALL pickup customers, not selectively.
Loyalty-programme overlap: cannot tie review request to loyalty-points award.
FTC Consumer Review Fairness Act 15 USC §45b — anti-disparagement gag clauses prohibited.
Pharmacy pickup: HIPAA — keep card copy generic, never reference prescription / medical context, offer to all customers (front-of-store + Rx).
Third-party-platform reviews: DoorDash / Uber Eats / Grubhub reviews are separate platforms; this card targets Google Business Profile only.

brief.label: Pickup programme economics + ROI
items: Per-bag-tag BOM: $0.30–$1.20 paper + NTAG213 or NFC sticker; $1.50–$3.00 PVC card variant.
Per-store cost: $50–$300 depending on bag-tag vs counter card mix + curbside variant.
Multi-location chain: $10K–$80K for 100–500 store estate (high-volume bag-tag consumption).
Review-velocity uplift: 4–8× post-rollout vs verbal-only or third-party-platform-only baseline.
Star-rating uplift: 4.0–4.3 → 4.4–4.7 within 3–4 months for consistently-deployed pickup chains.
BOPIS conversion correlation: 0.1 star uplift → 4–7 % increase in BOPIS-trial customers.
Reorder cycle: 3–6 months typical for bag-tag (high-consumption disposable).
Replacement reserve: 15–30 % per year (bag-tags travel home with customer).
Curbside variant: lower per-unit cost but higher loss rate (drive-thru vehicle interactions).

dataHighlight.heading: Bag-tag conversion at unboxing / first-bite moment
dataHighlight.text: Restaurant takeout, BOPIS retail, curbside grocery, pharmacy pickup, coffee mobile-order pickup-counter businesses running NFC bag-tags with runner verbal handoff at the order-confirmation moment consistently see 5–10 % conversion at point of bag-tag discovery (unboxing or first-bite at home / in car) vs 0.5–1 % for counter-card-only baseline. Review velocity uplift: 4–8× post-rollout. Star-rating uplift typically 4.0–4.3 → 4.4–4.7 within 3–4 months. BOPIS-trial uplift: 4–7 % per 0.1 star improvement. Mobile-order-platform integration spans Toast (counter-service), Olo (multi-restaurant brand aggregator), DoorDash / Uber Eats / Grubhub (third-party pickup), Square Online, Shopify POS (BOPIS), ChowNow, Manhattan Active Omni (enterprise OMS), Target Drive Up, Walmart+, Surescripts pharmacy. sections.title: Bag-tag + sticker mechanics — substrate, adhesive, attachment workflow
bullets: Bag-tag format — slip-in or staple-attached fabric tag (cardstock 250-350 gsm or fabric Tyvek 50-100 gsm) with embedded NTAG213 inlay (8mm or larger); attachment via slot-and-tab + staple + adhesive sticker.
Bag sticker format — peel-and-stick NFC sticker (NTAG213 inlay laminated to paper face + adhesive backing); applied directly to paper / plastic bag exterior; 1.5K-2K applications per roll.
Box / clamshell sticker — for restaurant takeout container (clamshell, pizza box, deli container); thermal-resistant adhesive survives hot food contact.
Bag-stuffer card — separate NFC card placed inside bag with order; thicker stock (PVC CR-80) durable + reusable for customer keepsake.
Receipt insert — pre-printed receipt with QR + 'Tap card at receipt-bottom' callout; lowest unit cost ($0.05-$0.20) but lowest conversion.
Take-home pamphlet — multi-page brochure with NFC chip + retention messaging; for high-LTV pickup (subscription meal box, monthly grocery delivery, prescription refill).
Window-decal at curbside — for vehicles arriving at curbside spot; staff applies decal to inside window during handoff; 3-5% sustained conversion.
Receipt-on-bag thermal label — POS thermal label printed on-demand at bag-fill time with order info + 'Tap to review' QR; integrated into existing print workflow at low marginal cost.
Attachment workflow — at order-bagging step: fold tag through bag handle / staple to bag opening / slip card inside bag; adds 2-5 seconds per order; staff training emphasises consistent placement.
Bag-tag survival rate — at-home discovery typically 70-85% (some bags discarded at car); decay over 7 days as bag is reused / discarded; review-tap window is typically 0-24 hours post-pickup.
Multi-format combo — bag-tag (travels home) + counter card (visible during wait) + curbside-runner handoff card (for drive-up) drives 3-8× review lift vs single placement.

Bag supplier integration — major bag suppliers (Inteplast, Genpak, Eco-Products, Karat, Solo Cup, Pactiv Evergreen) can pre-attach NFC sticker / tag during bag manufacture for high-volume operators; reduces per-order labour cost.
Compostable + recyclable considerations — bag + tag material must align with operator sustainability commitments; FSC paper + ASTM D6868 compostable + GRS recycled-content variants available.

Failure modes — staff forgets to attach (mitigated by integration into bag-fill SOP), tag falls off in transit (mitigated by stronger adhesive), bag discarded before discovery (cardstock + premium card survives), NFC chip damaged by water (mitigated by laminated waterproof substrate).

sections.title: BOPIS / curbside / drive-thru workflow integration — POS, OMS, app integration
bullets: BOPIS (Buy Online Pick-up In-Store) — customer orders online (web / app) → store picks order → customer arrives + presents pickup code → staff hands order + review-card / bag-tag.
Curbside pickup — customer arrives at designated stall → texts store via app → staff brings order to vehicle → review handoff at vehicle window; high satisfaction moment (low-friction).
Drive-thru pickup — customer orders at speaker → pulls forward → window staff hands order via window + review handoff; very fast handoff (5-15 seconds); high volume but lower per-order conversion.

Locker pickup — Amazon Hub Locker, Walmart Pickup Tower, grocery locker, USPS locker; customer scans QR / enters code → locker opens → customer takes order; lower review-engagement (no human touchpoint) — passive sticker on locker screen + receipt.

Delivery handoff — 3rd-party (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Instacart, Shipt) or in-house delivery; review prompt at delivery point + driver-handed card; less consistent than store-pickup but reaches different audience.

Order management integration — Manhattan Active Omni, Aptos OMS, IBM Sterling OMS, Salesforce Commerce Cloud OMS, Shopify Order Management, NetSuite OneWorld, Oracle Retail Order Management coordinate inventory + fulfillment + review automation.
POS integration — Toast, Square, Clover, Lightspeed, TouchBistro coordinate pickup + bag-tag fulfilment at restaurant; Shopify POS, Square Retail, Lightspeed Retail, Clover at retail.
Mobile app integration — operator app sends pickup-ready notification + post-pickup review prompt; common at Target Drive Up, Walmart Pickup, Chick-fil-A, Starbucks app, Domino's, Subway app.

In-app review request flow — customer arrives at pickup → app prompts 'Order ready! Tap here to review your experience' at pickup-confirmation moment; sometimes replaces physical handoff card; +3-8% mobile-app-attributed conversion.
Cross-channel attribution — UTM-tagged NFC card + per-order ID + customer cohort tracking attributes review to specific pickup event; surfaces in retailer analytics.

Margin economics — BOPIS lowers fulfilment cost (avoid last-mile shipping) while raising in-store engagement; margin lift typically 2-5% vs pure ship-to-customer; additional 5-15% in-store purchase rate at counter-pickup (impulse buy).
Pickup volume — Target reports 30-50% of online orders via Drive Up + Order Pickup + Same Day; Walmart similar; Chick-fil-A 60%+ of orders mobile-order-pickup; Domino's 70%+ digital.
Multi-channel routing — order routes to bag-tag (delivery) / pickup-card / drive-thru-runner card / locker-sticker based on fulfilment method; per-channel UTM differentiates analytics.
Order verification — pickup-staff verifies order identity (code, name, last-4 phone) → completes handoff + review prompt; verification step is brief satisfaction-peak moment for prompt.

sections.title: Vertical patterns — quick-service restaurant / fast-casual / grocery / pharmacy / retail / ghost kitchen
bullets: QSR (Quick-Service Restaurant: McDonald's, Burger King, Wendy's, Taco Bell, KFC, Subway, Chipotle, Panera Bread, Five Guys, In-N-Out) — drive-thru + counter pickup + delivery; bag-tag dominant; 2-5% sustained conversion; very high volume.
Fast-casual (Chipotle, Cava Group, Sweetgreen, Shake Shack, &pizza, Wingstop, BurgerFi, Mendocino Farms) — counter pickup + delivery + tabletop; bag-tag + counter card; 3-8% conversion.
Pizza chain (Domino's, Pizza Hut, Papa John's, Little Caesars, Papa Murphy's, Toppers) — pickup + delivery; box-sticker + bag-tag + delivery-handoff card; 3-7% conversion.
Sandwich + sub (Subway, Jersey Mike's, Firehouse Subs, Jimmy John's, Quiznos, Wawa, Sheetz) — counter pickup + delivery + bag-tag; 2-5% conversion.
Coffee + cafe (Starbucks, Dunkin', Tim Hortons, Peet's, Caribou, Dutch Bros) — counter pickup + drive-thru + mobile-order; cup-sleeve sticker + bag-tag; 2-5% conversion at very high volume.
Ghost kitchen + virtual brand (delivery-only restaurants on DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub) — bag-tag dominant (no physical storefront); 1-4% conversion via delivery-only.
Grocery (Kroger, Albertsons, Publix, Whole Foods, Sprouts, Wegmans, H-E-B) — Drive Up + Order Pickup + Same Day; bag-tag + curbside-runner card; 2-5% conversion at very high volume.

Pharmacy (Walgreens, CVS, Rite Aid, Walmart Pharmacy, Costco Pharmacy, supermarket pharmacy) — prescription pickup + curbside; bag-tag + counter card; HIPAA + state pharmacy board compliance required.

BOPIS retail (Target Drive Up, Walmart Pickup, Best Buy Same Day, Home Depot Pickup, Lowe's Pickup, Bed Bath & Beyond, DSW, Nordstrom) — designated pickup counter + curbside + locker; per-channel conversion 2-8%.
Specialty retail (Apple Store, Microsoft Store, B&H, Adorama) — Genius Bar pickup + service pickup; 4-10% conversion.
Wine + liquor (Total Wine, BevMo, ABC Fine Wine, local liquor stores) — pickup + delivery; bag-tag + counter card; age-verification overlay.
Pet supply (Chewy, PetSmart, Petco Pickup, BarkShop) — pickup + delivery; bag-tag + post-purchase email; pet-emotional cohort drives higher conversion.
Convenience + gas station (7-Eleven, Wawa, Sheetz, Circle K, Casey's General Stores) — fuel-pump + in-store pickup; bag-tag + receipt; 1-3% conversion at very high volume.
Cannabis dispensary (state-licensed) — pickup + delivery; bag-tag + state-compliance overlay (age-verification, state-specific advertising rules).
Restaurant delivery handoff (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Instacart driver) — driver-handed card at customer door; per-driver attribution drives 2-5% conversion.

sections.title: Compliance + sensitive pickup categories — HIPAA pharmacy / age-verification / state law overlays
bullets: Pharmacy pickup HIPAA — prescription pickup involves PHI (Protected Health Information); HIPAA Marketing Rule 45 CFR § 164.508 requires patient authorization for marketing using PHI. Generic review card (no patient name + medication on card) qualifies for face-to-face exception or promotional-gift-of-nominal-value exception.

What's allowed at pharmacy — generic NFC card given to all pharmacy customers at counter (no PHI on card design or distribution); passive sticker at pharmacy counter; staff verbal prompt 'We'd appreciate your honest feedback on Google'.

What's prohibited — review-request SMS using prescription identity ('Hi John, you picked up your statin medication today...'); patient-name + medication-specific card; segmenting prompts based on diagnosis category.
Substance use disorder pharmacy (42 CFR Part 2) — more restrictive; methadone clinic + buprenorphine prescription requires explicit consent for marketing communications; passive prompt only.
Age-verification — alcohol + cannabis + tobacco pickup requires age-verification overlay; review prompt at age-verified pickup moment; state-specific rules apply.
State pharmacy board — California Board of Pharmacy, Texas State Board of Pharmacy, New York Board of Pharmacy + 50-state boards regulate pharmacy advertising + patient interaction.

Cannabis dispensary state compliance — California Bureau of Cannabis Control, Colorado MED, Washington WSLCB + state-by-state advertising rules; some states prohibit any cannabis advertising; review prompts subject to state-specific restrictions.
Tobacco + vape — FDA Center for Tobacco Products regulates tobacco advertising; state laws layer additional restrictions; review prompts at vape shop subject to varying rules.
Alcohol — state ABC + alcohol-control commission regulates; review prompts at liquor store + bar pickup subject to state-specific rules.
Food allergen + recall — pickup workflows must accommodate allergen labeling + recall notifications; review prompt at allergen-restricted pickup must not interfere with safety communication.
FDA food safety — restaurant pickup subject to FDA Food Code + state health department; review prompts cannot interfere with food safety + temperature compliance.

Compliant prompt language — 'If you had a good experience, we'd appreciate your honest feedback on Google' (passive + truthful + non-incentivised + all-customers-asked); avoid 'Loved your prescription? Tap for 5 stars' (HIPAA + FTC violation).

Audit trail — pickup-counter operator should document compliant prompt language + staff training + no-PHI-on-card policy + age-verification protocol + food-safety integration; defensible in HHS OCR + state board + FDA inquiry.

Multi-state operators — chain operators in 50 states must layer state-specific compliance overlays; corporate compliance team establishes lowest-common-denominator language + per-state addendum where needed.

faq.question: When is the highest-converting moment to prompt for a pickup-counter review?
faq.answer: The bag-tag discovery moment — when the customer opens the bag at home / in the car and sees the tag at first-bite or unboxing. The bag-tag does the work after the customer leaves, removing in-counter awkwardness for time-pressed pickup customers. Bag-tag + runner verbal handoff converts 5–10% vs 0.5–1% for passive counter-card-only. The 3–5 second verbal window is at order-verification handoff, not before.

faq.question: How does this differ from the retail checkout-counter solution?
faq.answer: Pickup customers don't browse counter signage — they want a fast handoff and exit. So bag-tag (travels home) + runner-card (curbside drive-up) replace the POS-adjacent counter card geometry of the retail checkout context. Conversion happens at unboxing rather than at counter. Compliance overlay shifts: pharmacy-pickup HIPAA generic-copy + restaurant no-discount-tie-in are pickup-specific concerns. See /solutions/google-review-cards-for-checkout-counters/ for full-service POS-counter venues.

faq.question: What about curbside / drive-thru pickup customers who never enter the store?
faq.answer: Curbside requires a different placement: runner-handed card (driver hands card to customer through window with bag) or curbside-bag-clip attached to bag handle. Drive-thru pharmacy + drive-thru restaurant variants use the same runner-handoff pattern. Counter-card geometry doesn't reach curbside customers. Track per-runner card-handoff KPI for curbside-shift staffing analytics.

faq.question: What HIPAA considerations apply to pharmacy prescription pickup?
faq.answer: If the review prompt references the customer's prescription or medical context, HIPAA may apply. Best practice for pharmacy pickup: keep card copy generic ('Thanks for picking up with us — tap if you have a moment to share'), do not reference specific prescription / medical context, and offer the prompt to ALL pickup customers (front-of-store retail + prescription pickup customers). The pharmacy clinical workflow is a separate context — see /solutions/google-review-cards-for-clinics/ for HIPAA-aware clinical-side prompts.

faq.question: What's the right reorder cycle for pickup-counter bag-tags?
faq.answer: 3–6 months typical for bag-tags (high-consumption disposable; tags travel home with customer). Replacement reserve runs 15–30% per year — much higher than counter-card programmes because bag-tags don't return to store. Reorder synced to bag-supplier reorder cycle. Multi-location chains coordinate central reorder + bag-supplier pre-attachment integration where feasible.

faq.question: Which bag-tag attachment method works best — staple, slot, sticker, or pre-attached?
faq.answer: Slot-and-tab fold-through-handle works for paper bags + Tyvek (no equipment needed, 2-3 sec per tag, clean appearance). Staple attachment is fastest at high volume (1-2 sec per tag, requires desktop stapler) but creates small hole risk. Adhesive sticker direct on bag exterior is simplest (peel-and-stick, 1-2 sec) but lower visibility. Box / clamshell sticker for restaurant takeout (clamshell, pizza box) uses thermal-resistant adhesive surviving hot food. Pre-attached at bag manufacture (Inteplast, Genpak, Eco-Products, Karat, Solo Cup, Pactiv Evergreen) eliminates per-order labour but requires high-volume commitment + 8-12 week bag-supply lead time. Bag-tag survival rate 70-85% at-home discovery; tap window typically 0-24 hours post-pickup. Multi-format combo (bag-tag + counter card + curbside runner card) drives 3-8× review lift vs single placement.

faq.question: How does BOPIS / curbside / drive-thru change the review workflow?
faq.answer: Each fulfilment channel needs different review-card geometry. BOPIS counter pickup: bag-tag + counter card + receipt insert; 4-10% conversion. Curbside (Target Drive Up, Walmart Pickup, grocery, restaurant): runner hands order at vehicle window + bag-tag travels home; 5-12% conversion (high satisfaction, low friction). Drive-thru (McDonald's, Chick-fil-A, Starbucks): window staff hands bag-tag during very fast 5-15 sec handoff; 2-5% conversion at high volume. Locker pickup (Amazon Hub, Walmart Pickup Tower, grocery locker): no human touchpoint — passive sticker on locker screen + receipt; 2-4% conversion. Delivery (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Instacart): driver-handed card at customer door; 2-5% conversion + reach different audience than store-pickup. Order management integration (Manhattan Active Omni, Aptos OMS, IBM Sterling, Salesforce, Shopify, NetSuite, Oracle Retail) coordinates fulfilment + review automation. Mobile app integration (Target, Walmart, Chick-fil-A, Starbucks, Domino's, Subway) sends in-app review prompt at pickup-confirmation.

faq.question: What sensitive-pickup categories need special compliance handling?
faq.answer: Pharmacy pickup involves HIPAA — generic NFC card (no patient name + medication on card) qualifies for face-to-face exception or promotional-gift-of-nominal-value exception under 45 CFR § 164.508. Avoid SMS using prescription identity. Substance use disorder pharmacy (42 CFR Part 2) is more restrictive — methadone + buprenorphine require explicit consent for marketing. Age-verification pickups (alcohol, cannabis, tobacco, vape) overlay state-specific advertising rules — California Bureau of Cannabis Control, Colorado MED, Washington WSLCB, state ABC commissions, FDA Center for Tobacco Products. Cannabis dispensary state compliance varies wildly — some states prohibit cannabis advertising entirely; review prompts subject to per-state restrictions. State pharmacy boards (California, Texas, New York + 50-state boards) regulate pharmacy interaction language. Food allergen + recall workflows must not be interfered with by review prompts. FDA Food Code + state health department supervises restaurant pickup. Compliant prompt language: 'If you had a good experience, we'd appreciate your honest feedback on Google' — passive + truthful + non-incentivised + all-customers-asked. Multi-state operators layer state-specific compliance overlays + lowest-common-denominator corporate language.
